mainTopic: Whether moving by oxen counts as 'carrying' for the boat law of חנניא; the wagon and chest categories of טומאה; the ברייתא on מדרס of earthenware and ships (רב זביד vs. רב פפא); and the source that a כלי חרס cannot become impure through מדרס.
overview: The גמרא continues the discussion of the Jordan boat. חנניא holds that a boat can become impure because it is moved both full and empty. The גמרא asks whether being moved by oxen counts as being carried, and proves that it does from a משנה about three types of wagons, which it quotes along with that משנה's list of three types of chests. Next comes a ברייתא: an earthenware vessel does not become impure through מדרס, and רבי יוסי says 'even the ship.' רב זביד explains this one way, רב פפא objects from the word 'אף', and רב פפא offers a reading in which רבי יוסי follows חנניא. The גמרא then asks for the source that a כלי חרס is immune to מדרס. חזקיה and דבי רבי ישמעאל each bring a פסוק comparing the bed to the person: only something that can be purified in a מקוה can become a מדרס. Finally, רבי אילעא begins an objection from a teaching about a reed mat, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does moving by oxen count as carrying for חנניא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, according to חנניא, being moved by oxen counts as being 'carried'.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to חנניא, is being moved by oxen considered 'carrying'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about חנניא's view on the Jordan boat. This sets up the next step, where it will bring a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנניא compares the boat to a sack, which can become impure because it is carried both full and empty. A loaded boat on land is not lifted by hand. It is dragged by oxen. So the question is whether that kind of movement counts as the 'carrying' the comparison needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it called / is it considered

phrases.english: And according to Ḥananya, carrying by means of oxen,
phrases.notes: Refers back to חנניא in the משנה about the Jordan boat

phrases.english: is it considered carrying?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַחֲנַנְיָא טִילְטוּל עַל יְדֵי שְׁוָורִים שְׁמֵיהּ טִילְטוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a question on חנניא's view in the earlier משנה about the Jordan boat
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether being moved by oxen meets the 'carried full and empty' requirement in חנניא's reasoning

steps.title: Yes: proof from the three types of wagons
steps.stepSummary: Yes, moving by oxen counts. A משנה teaches that a stone wagon, which oxen pull, can still become טמא מת according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as we learned: there are three types of wagons. One made like a chair can become impure through מדרס. One made like a bed can become impure from a corpse. One made of stones is completely pure. And רבי יוחנן said: if it has a space that can hold pomegranates, it can become impure from a corpse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers 'yes' and proves it from a משנה about wagons, together with רבי יוחנן's comment on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wagon is never carried by hand. Oxen pull it. Yet רבי יוחנן says a stone wagon that can hold pomegranates can become impure from a corpse. This shows that being moved by oxen counts as the kind of carrying needed for a vessel to receive טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A chair with sides; a seat
Impurity from a זב sitting or lying on an item
A receptacle; a space that can hold things

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מדרס and טמא מת. An item that is 'טמאה מדרס' can become impure just from a זב sitting on it. An item that is 'טמאה טמא מת' can receive other types of impurity, but not מדרס.

phrases.english: Yes, as we learned in a mishna:
There are three types of wagons.
One made like a chair can become impure through treading.
phrases.notes: It is made for sitting, so a זב sitting on it makes it impure

phrases.english: One made like a bed can become impure with corpse impurity.
One made for stones is pure from any impurity.
phrases.notes: Its bottom is like a net with large holes, so it does not count as a container

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל רִמּוֹנִים,
phrases.english: And if it has a receptacle that can hold pomegranates,
phrases.notes: The holes are small enough that a pomegranate would not fall through

phrases.english: it can become impure with corpse impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with a proof from a משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Moving by oxen counts as carrying, as shown by a wagon pulled by oxen that can still receive טומאה
steps.raayaObject: That moving by oxen counts as carrying for the laws of טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the three wagons, together with רבי יוחנן's comment about a receptacle for pomegranates
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps חנניא's view consistent. A boat moved by oxen on land can count as 'carried full and empty,' just like a sack.

steps.title: The rest of the משנה: three types of chests
steps.stepSummary: The same משנה lists three types of chests: side-opening (מדרס), top-opening (טמא מת), and very large (pure).
steps.simpleTranslation: There are three types of chests. A chest that opens from its side can become impure through מדרס. One that opens from the top can become impure from a corpse. And one that is very large is pure from everything.
steps.whatsHappening: Since it just quoted the wagon משנה, the גמרא also quotes its second half, about chests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A chest that opens from the side can be used without the person sitting on it getting up, so it counts as a seat and receives מדרס. A chest that opens from the top makes the sitter get up, so it is not a seat, but it is still a vessel. A very large chest, over forty סאה, is not a movable vessel at all, so it stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Its opening is on its side
One that comes in a large measure (over forty סאה)

phrases.english: There are three types of chests:
A chest whose opening is on its side can become impure through treading.
phrases.notes: One can open it while still sitting on it

phrases.english: One that opens from the top can become impure with corpse impurity.
And one that comes in a large size is pure from any impurity.
phrases.notes: It holds forty סאה or more

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה by association
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Side-opening chest receives מדרס; top-opening chest receives only טמא מת and the like; a very large chest is completely pure

steps.title: ברייתא: earthenware is immune to מדרס, 'even the ship'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an earthenware vessel does not become impure through מדרס. רבי יוסי adds: 'even the ship.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: an earthenware vessel is pure from מדרס. רבי יוסי says: even the ship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a short and unclear ברייתא. This sets up the next steps, which will try to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half is clear: a זב sitting on a כלי חרס does not make it impure. But רבי יוסי's words, 'even the ship,' do not say whether the ship is pure or impure. That gap is what the גמרא will try to fill.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Regarding treading, an earthenware vessel is pure.
Rabbi Yosei says: even the ship.
phrases.notes: He does not say whether he means 'pure' or 'impure'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן מִדְרַס כְּלִי חֶרֶס טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new source related to the ship discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כלי חרס does not become impure through מדרס; רבי יוסי adds something about a ship

steps.title: What is the ברייתא saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of the unclear ברייתא. This sets up רב זביד's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not clear how a ship fits with earthenware, or whether 'אף' makes the ship pure or impure. The question asks for the full meaning.

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the ברייתא in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The intended meaning of the ברייתא, especially רבי יוסי's 'even the ship'

steps.title: רב זביד: the earthenware ship is impure for the תנא קמא, pure for רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד explains: the תנא קמא says an earthenware ship is impure, like חנניא. רבי יוסי says the ship is pure, like our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said, this is what it means: an earthenware vessel is pure from מדרס but becomes impure through touching. And an earthenware ship is impure, like חנניא. רבי יוסי says: even the ship is pure, like the תנא of our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד fills in the missing words of the ברייתא and turns it into a dispute about an earthenware ship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the תנא קמא follows חנניא and makes an earthenware ship impure. רבי יוסי follows our משנה and makes the ship pure. So the two תנאים disagree directly.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying
Like the תנא of our משנה

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said, this is what it is saying:
Regarding treading, an earthenware vessel is pure,
but regarding its contact, it is impure,
and an earthenware ship is impure, in accordance with Ḥananya.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף הַסְּפִינָה טְהוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: even the ship is pure,
in accordance with the tanna of our mishna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by filling in the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא holds an earthenware ship is impure like חנניא; רבי יוסי holds it is pure like our משנה

steps.title: רב פפא objects: what does 'אף' mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רב זביד: the word 'אף' (even) means adding, but in רב זביד's reading רבי יוסי is disagreeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: what is the meaning of 'even'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רב זביד's reading from the wording of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אף' means 'also, like the previous case.' But in רב זביד's reading, the תנא קמא says the ship is impure and רבי יוסי says it is pure. That is a disagreement, not an addition, so the word 'אף' does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Even / also (adds to what came before)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objects to this:
What is the meaning of 'even'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא מַאי אַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב זביד's explanation in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זביד's reading of רבי יוסי's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אף' signals agreement and addition, but רב זביד makes רבי יוסי disagree with the תנא קמא

steps.title: רב פפא's reading: wood is impure, and רבי יוסי adds the ship
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reads the ברייתא so that the תנא קמא mentions wooden vessels as impure, rules the Jordan ship pure, and רבי יוסי adds the ship to the impure list, like חנניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said, this is what it means: an earthenware vessel is pure from מדרס but impure through touching. A wooden vessel is impure both through מדרס and through touching. And the Jordan ship is pure, like our משנה. רבי יוסי says: even the ship is impure, like חנניא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new reading in which the word 'אף' makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא mentions wooden vessels as impure. רבי יוסי's 'even the ship' adds the Jordan ship to that impure category, so 'אף' is a true addition. This also means רבי יוסי follows חנניא, while the תנא קמא follows our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jordan ship, a small river boat

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא: the תנא קמא holds the Jordan ship is pure, like our משנה. רבי יוסי holds it is impure, like חנניא. The word 'אף' adds the ship to the wooden vessels that are impure.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הָכִי קָאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said, this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: מִדְרַס כְּלִי חֶרֶס — טָהוֹר, וּמַגָּעוֹ טָמֵא.
phrases.english: Regarding treading, an earthenware vessel is pure, and regarding its contact, it is impure.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל עֵץ, בֵּין מִדְרָסוֹ וּבֵין מַגָּעוֹ — טָמֵא,
phrases.english: And a wooden vessel, both regarding its treading and its contact, is impure,
and the Jordan ship is pure, in accordance with the tanna of our mishna.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף הַסְּפִינָה טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: even the ship is impure,
phrases.notes: Like the other wooden vessels just listed

phrases.english: in accordance with Ḥananya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב זביד's reading in response to the objection in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the ברייתא by adding a clause about wooden vessels
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב זביד: the ברייתא is about an earthenware ship, with רבי יוסי disagreeing
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא lists wooden vessels as impure, and רבי יוסי adds the Jordan ship to them, following חנניא

steps.title: Where do we learn that earthenware is immune to מדרס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a כלי חרס does not become impure through מדרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that an earthenware vessel is pure from מדרס?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the ברייתא and asks for its source. This sets up חזקיה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earthenware vessel can become impure through contact. So why should a זב sitting on it not make it impure? The גמרא wants a פסוק for this rule.

phrases.english: And regarding treading on an earthenware vessel, from where do we derive that it is pure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening ruling of the ברייתא to find its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a כלי חרס cannot receive מדרס

steps.title: חזקיה: the bed is compared to the person, so it must be purifiable in a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה learns from 'ואיש אשר יגע במשכבו' that a bed is compared to the person. Just as he can be purified in a מקוה, only an item that can be purified in a מקוה receives מדרס. Earthenware cannot, so it is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: the פסוק says 'And a man who touches his bed.' The פסוק compares his bed to him. Just as he can become pure in a מקוה, so too his bed must be something that can become pure in a מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers with a פסוק and a היקש that compares the bed to the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק puts 'man' and 'his bed' together, the bed must share the man's quality of being purifiable in a מקוה. An impure earthenware vessel can only be purified by breaking it, not by immersion. So it cannot become a 'משכב' that receives מדרס.

keyTerms.meaning: His bed (an item that receives מדרס)
Purification through immersion in a ritual bath

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי חרס does not receive מדרס because only items that can be purified in a מקוה, like the person himself, are included in 'משכבו'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This היקש sets a general rule: an item can receive מדרס only if it can be purified in a מקוה. This explains the first line of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiya said: as the verse states:
'And a man who touches his bed' (ויקרא 15:5),
it juxtaposes his bed to himself:

phrases.aramaic: מָה הוּא אִית לֵיהּ טׇהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶה —
phrases.english: just as he has purification in a ritual bath,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִשְׁכָּבוֹ נָמֵי אִית לֵיהּ טׇהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶה.
phrases.english: so too his bed must also have purification in a ritual bath.
phrases.notes: Earthenware cannot be purified in a מקוה, so it is excluded

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש compares the bed to the person: only items that can be purified in a מקוה receive מדרס, which excludes earthenware

steps.title: School of רבי ישמעאל: A second source from the woman's bed
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל learn from 'כמשכב נדתה יהיה לה' that her bed is compared to her. Just as she can be purified in a מקוה, only a bed that can be purified in a מקוה receives מדרס, so כלי חרס is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'like the bed of her נדה period it shall be for her.' The פסוק compares her bed to her. Just as she can become pure in a מקוה, her bed must also be something that can become pure in a מקוה. This leaves out a כלי חרס, which cannot become pure in a מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question of Step 9, this time from the school of רבי ישמעאל, using a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה compared the bed to the man (a זב). דבי רבי ישמעאל compare the bed to the woman (a זבה). The logic is the same: the bed must be like the person, who can be purified in a מקוה, and a כלי חרס cannot be purified that way, so it never becomes a מדרס.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study hall) of רבי ישמעאל
Compares or links two things (a היקש), so they share the same rules
Her bed, meaning the thing she lies on

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources teach the same rule. חזקיה compares the bed to the man, and דבי רבי ישמעאל compare the bed to the woman. In both, the bed must be able to become pure in a מקוה, so a כלי חרס cannot become a מדרס.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule that רבי אילעא is about to challenge: impurity of a 'bed' depends on whether the item can be purified in a מקוה.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Like the bed of her menstrual period it shall be for her"
It compares her bed to her:

phrases.aramaic: מָה הִיא אִית לַהּ טׇהֳרָה בְּמִקְוֶה —
phrases.english: Just as she can be purified in a ritual bath,
so too her bed also
must be something that can be purified in a ritual bath,
to exclude an earthenware vessel,
which cannot be purified in a ritual bath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel second source for the same rule חזקיה derived in Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כלי חרס does not receive מדרס because the bed is compared to the זבה, and like her it must be able to be purified in a מקוה.

steps.title: רבי אילעא opens a challenge about a reed mat
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא begins an objection by quoting a source that asks: where do we learn that a reed mat (מפץ) becomes impure through a dead body?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא raised an objection: From where do we learn that a reed mat becomes impure from a dead body?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא starts a challenge to the rule we just learned. The גמרא is setting up the next move, and the full challenge will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מתיב tells us that this is an attack, even though the line looks like a simple question. רבי אילעא is about to quote a teaching about a reed mat that seems to conflict with the rule 'only what can be purified in a מקוה becomes impure as a bed.' For now, we only have the opening question.

keyTerms.meaning: Through contact with a dead body (טומאת מת)
From where do we know? Asking for a source

steps.confusionAlert: Even though this line is phrased as a question (מנין), it is not a simple request for information. The word מתיב shows that רבי אילעא is quoting this source in order to attack the rule from Steps 10–11.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ila raised an objection:
From where do we know that a reed mat becomes impure from a corpse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an objection against the rule derived in Steps 10–11
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only items purifiable in a מקוה can receive מדרס, which is why כלי חרס is excluded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: רבי אילעא introduces a ברייתא about a reed mat and טומאת מת, whose continuation will be used to challenge the rule.
